jobs.title: Environmental Project Manager - Remediation - 6 years min experience
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is actively seeking a talented Environmental Project/Program Manager for immediate employment in our Oakland, California office. In this role, you will be making a positive impact in the community through rewarding projects within our Environmental Practices.

This hybrid position (office and remote) requires the ideal candidate to demonstrate experience in regulatory and client engagement on complex sites, as well as investigation and remediation project experience, all while maintaining a strong emphasis on health and safety. The candidate should be detail-oriented, possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, and be capable of working independently while collaborating within a high-performance team.

Working at AECOM means being part of a global team and collaborating with award-winning professionals worldwide. In this position, you will also be responsible for supporting business development for the Oakland office, technical delivery, stakeholder engagement and communication, and financial management.

Responsibilities for this position may include the following:

Project/Program Management:

Oversee the management of projects, assisting in the establishment of project-specific objectives and policies.
Oversee the management the program for the portfolio of projects, assisting in the establishment of program specific processes and procedures.
Understand site investigation and remediation techniques to drive effective solutions for our utility client.
Engage with existing and potential clients to discuss AECOM service capabilities and expand the services provided.
Ensure all aspects of the project portfolio align with design, budget, and schedule requirements.
Provide technical oversight and quality control throughout the project lifecycle.
Define project scope and objectives clearly.
Manage all phases of projects from initiation to closeout.
Anticipate resource needs and manage resources effectively.
Exercise decision-making authority while recognizing risks and uncertainties, implementing plans to mitigate them.
Provide consistent project updates to various stakeholders regarding strategy, adjustments, and progress.
Identify, mitigate, and manage project risks effectively.
Manage complex client relationships and projects.
Consistently deliver profit margins as planned.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

BS in engineering, geology, environmental science, or a related field with 6+ years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
US Citizen or US Permanent Resident. Sponsorship at this time or in the future is not eligible for this role.
This role is subject to a background check.

Preferred Qualifications:

10+ years of experience in site investigation, remediation, project management, and business development.
2+ years of experience managing a portfolio of projects and leading a team for a major client.
Licensed in the State of California (Professional Engineer or Geologist).
Experience working with state regulatory agencies in the states referenced for licensure.
Proven experience in scheduling resources to ensure timely and budget-compliant project delivery.
Background in business development.
Current 40-hour HAZWOPER certification, including 8-hour Supervisor training.
PMP certification.
Experience with regulatory and stakeholder negotiations.
Proven track record of successfully managing environmental projects for various types of clients.
Detail-oriented with strong organizational and communication skills, both verbal and written.
Superior communication, writing, editing, and reporting skills for diverse audiences.
Experience preparing proposals, cost estimates, schedules, and change orders.

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $125000 to $155000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Water Resources Market Leader
jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re looking for a place to advance your career, where you can contribute to a dynamic innovative firm, tackle demanding project work, and collaborate with industry recognized professionals – Geosyntec Consultants is the place for you!

Geosyntec
is seeking a Principal level Water Resources Market Leader
to join our growing national Water Resources Practice, based out of our Los Angeles, CA
;
San Diego, CA;
Sacramento, CA; Lakewood, CO
or any of our other U.S. based offices. The potential to work remotely from your home-office is available at the discretion of the Company. This is a unique opportunity to join a leadership team actively engaged in growing the water business at Geosyntec. This position will be responsible for developing and implementing a strategy for achieving significant market share for Geosyntec in the Water Resources market area.

As a senior member of our Water Resources practice, you lead complex water resources projects around water supply management, water rights permitting, and groundwater / surface water management. As a market leader, you will be responsible for a combination of technical project execution, client relationship management and water resource subject matter expertise, task and team leadership, while actively engaging existing and new client opportunities from a business development growth standpoint. Our Water Resources group works on complex projects ranging from water supply development, water supply management, water rights, mining hydrogeology, contaminant hydrogeology, regulatory permitting, and source water protection, across the U.S.; In this role, you will have the opportunity to build and lead a team of experienced professionals, contribute to complex technical project work, as well as actively engage in growth and business development strategy.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic business planning to segment and target specific industrial, commercial and municipal clients for projects such as water supply, groundwater and surface water modeling, water availability, use and re-use, as well as regulatory considerations for water rights permitting; focused on the West Region Water Resources market;
Engagement with project and operations staff to align Geosyntec’s full service delivery capabilities with market demands;
Serve in the capacity of a Client Account Manager on selected accounts deemed critical to Geosyntec’s Water Resources market;
Active participation in professional societies, conferences, and meetings that will increase the visibility of the firm to potential clients and recruits. Make contributions to the profession that will result in individual recognition as an industry leader;
Project directorship, including ensuring client expectations are understood and met, budgets are adhered to, quality objectives are met, and follow-on work is attainted – Strategically related to; local scale hydrogeologic analyses for water supply management, regulatory compliance and new source development; modeling studies of aquifer systems; installation and testing of groundwater supply wells (and monitoring wells), aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) and surface recharge basin projects, and permitting and regulatory compliance projects, including water rights;
Recruiting, managing, and mentoring junior staff and mid-career engineers and scientists;
Reviewing and leading the preparation of major proposals;
Providing senior leadership subject matter expertise in meetings with clients, regulatory personnel, and other parties;
Technical Project delivery and project-manager responsibility for scoping, performing, managing, and delivering multiple concurrent project assignments;
Preparing technical reports, letters, memoranda, plans, specifications, and proposals
Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor's degree in Water Resources, Hydrogeology, Civil, Environmental or related engineering discipline with emphasis on water resources. (required)
Advanced degree in the same/similar (preferred)
Professional registration (i.e., PE, CHG) (required)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At least 10 years (15+ preferred) of direct water resources, hydrogeology, or engineering consulting experience working on water resource, contaminated sites, and mining projects; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Experience with multi-disciplinary project teams. (required)
Demonstrated success in project management, sales, and business development. (required)
Excellent leadership and detail-orientation skills. (required)
Experience with design and implementation of field hydrogeology programs in glacial, basalt, and clastic aquifer systems (required)
Experience with numerical modeling of groundwater flow and well test analysis (preferred).
Ability and willingness to perform fieldwork and travel as needed. (required)
Health & Safety training, medical monitoring, and client-driven drug and background testing may be required.
Valid U.S. driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

This opportunity will be posted for at least five days. The typical base salary range for this position is just one component of Geosyntec’s total compensation package for employees. Actual compensation will be determined based on education, experience, skill set and location.

jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Company

Trinity Consultants’ Monitoring Services team is hiring a Senior Air Quality Specialist to install, maintain, and troubleshoot ambient air quality and meteorological monitoring networks for clients across the country. This is a hands-on, field-first role for someone who takes pride in precise, defensible data. You’ll work directly with clients, travel to active monitoring sites, and be trusted to make real-time calls on equipment and data quality.

Schedule & Travel

Hybrid role based between the office and the field; ability to travel 2–5 days a week (transportation provided or compensated). Monday–Friday schedule; occasional weekend work may be required.

Field Operations & Installation

Conduct onsite installation, startup, and commissioning of meteorological and ambient air quality monitoring equipment.
Draw upon hands-on technical experience to perform analyzer maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibrations at remote monitoring sites, minimizing downtime and data loss.
Collect and operate time-integrated samples, and provide proper chain-of-custody documentation to analytical laboratories.
Apply practical field experience to support the design, integration, and build-out of ambient air quality monitoring systems.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

Maintain current audit and calibration certifications, and apply working knowledge of EPA and state monitoring protocols in the field.
Provide QA of air quality audit and calibration reports.
Review incoming data with an experienced eye to proactively flag instrumentation issues before they affect data quality.
Provide proper documentation and record keeping for all air quality systems and network servicing and auditing.

Client & Program Support

Provide meteorological sensor and air quality instrument calibration, maintenance, and audit services for numerous clients across the U.S., with a concentration in California.

Qualifications

4–8+ years of hands-on field experience in ambient air quality or meteorological monitoring; a Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, meteorology, or engineering may be considered in place of equivalent field experience.

Required Skills

Demonstrated, practical experience with DC electronics, telemetry, and remote data logging equipment.
Working knowledge of state and Federal (EPA) environmental monitoring guidelines and regulations, gained through direct application at active monitoring sites.
Hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience.
Strong work ethic, attention to detail, and proven problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Skills

Proven, hands-on experience operating and maintaining meteorological and air quality instrumentation.
Experience-based client interaction and communication skills, including strong active listening developed through direct client-facing field work.
Proficiency in the MS365 ecosystem (Teams, SharePoint, OneNote, etc.).

Pay range and compensation package

Our Santa Clarita office offers the stability of a corporate company with the atmosphere and camaraderie of a small, family-run business. We’re intentional about cultivating a fun, healthy environment for our team.

Competitive pay
401(k)
Dental insurance
Health insurance
Life insurance
Paid time off
Paid travel time, expenses, and daily per diem

Equal Opportunity Statement

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of duties. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to lift 70 lbs, travel freely and frequently, and remain on feet for up to 12 hours per day at field sites; multi-day field efforts are not uncommon. While performing site work, employees may occasionally be exposed to moving mechanical parts, high or precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, and toxic or caustic chemicals. Noise levels at monitoring sites are typically moderate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken. Comfort with basic math and algebra as applied to air quality measurements (percentages, area, volume, and similar calculations). Sound judgment interpreting instructions and troubleshooting variable field conditions where standardization is limited.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower all of our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

Our pledge to you

Join GHD

That’s the #PowerOfCommittment

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Are you ready to lead a dynamic team of Emergency Response/Preparedness and environmental professionals in tackling some of the most pressing challenges facing our environment today?

Who are we looking for?

As a Project Manager
at GHD, you will not only mentor and guide the team but also take the reins in environmental emergencies, collaborating closely with clients and agencies to ensure effective response and resolution.

Your role will extend beyond project management to include business development and client expansion activities, where your expertise in environmental engineering, geology, or related fields will shine. With 5+ years of project management experience under your belt, including a proven track record in emergency response, client relationship management, and business development, you'll bring a wealth of knowledge to the table.

From conducting environmental sampling and monitoring to spearheading regional visibility initiatives, your passion for environmental stewardship and problem-solving will drive our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, possess exceptional communication skills, and are committed to making a difference, join us in shaping a sustainable future. Apply today and Join our Emergency Management (GHD FIRST) team.

This opportunity can be based out of the Chicago office.

Who is GHD FIRST:

GHD Fast Incident Response Services Team (GHD FIRST) delivers turnkey, 24/7/365 incident response and management services throughout North America. The GHD FIRST team provides the following core services:

Emergency Preparedness, Planning, and Drills
Environmental/ Remediation Services
Incident Management / Incident Command System (ICS)
Air Monitoring/ Industrial Hygiene
Waste Management
Toxicology/ Risk Assessment
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)/ Database
Shoreline Clean-up Assessment Technique (SCAT)
Digital Technology/ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Services
Construction/ Construction Management Services
Crisis Communication and Community Engagement
Litigation Support

GHD has more than 100 offices across North America with over 500 staff trained in emergency response and emergency management procedures. Listed below is a management role currently open to grow and further develop the GHD FIRST business sector within GHD.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Accountable for one or more medium-sized projects of low to moderate complexity with a small- to medium-sized team. Focus on the creation of the project vision and planning documents and manage the implementation, reporting, and performance of the overall project with the expectation of delivering on time, within budget, and to scope.

Document Preparation: Prepare moderately complex documents using a variety of applications for technology devices, such as standard office software. Also responsible for gathering and summarizing data for reports.
Stakeholder Management: Plan and deliver stakeholder engagement activities to develop effective working relationships for projects and to ensure that stakeholder needs and concerns are identified and met.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Continuous Improvement: Contribute to reviewing existing operations in own area of work, and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements.
Work Scheduling and Allocation: Assign short-term work schedules to a team of subordinates in order to achieve expectations while following established timelines.
Project Assurance: Conduct assurance reviews within the project, facilitate the delivery of assurance reviews by independent third parties, and take appropriate action to resolve any issues identified, so that senior stakeholders have confidence that the project can deliver according to time, budget, and quality.
Project Scope Definition: Manage the delivery of research, workshops, and other activities to support the specification and agreement of project deliverables.
Project Planning: Produce workstream or project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, are appropriately organized to deliver project objectives, and comply with the organization's project management framework.
Project Reporting and Review: Draft project review reports and presentations, including key information, commentary, and recommendations, to support the review process and enable stakeholders to evaluate progress and agree on change.
Project Resource Management: Manage the deployment of project resources, proactively managing project costs, providing forecasts, and presenting variances with narrative at appropriate review points to ensure effective utilization.
Project Risk and Issue Management: Identify and evaluate risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints associated with the project, escalating matters where appropriate. Where necessary, develop, agree on, and implement solutions to overcome these concerns.
Project Closeout and Handover: Draft elements of product documentation and user training to support handover to business as usual. Contribute to post-project reviews and identification of lessons learned.
Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.
Willingness to respond to call outs during non-routine working hours
Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or a related field

Experience

General Experience: Experience enables job holder to deal with the majority of situations and to advise others (Over 3 years to 6 years)
Managerial Experience: Experience of general supervision of more junior colleagues (7 to 12 months)
Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA
Experience with railroad and pipeline related emergencies a plus

Benefits:

401K - Employees are eligible to participate on the first day of the month following 3 months of service
Paid time off – Our PTO benefit is designed to provide eligible employees with a period of rest and relaxation, sick, and personal time throughout the year. PTO starts at 16 days per year and increases with years of service
Holiday Pay - Holiday pay is provided for eligible employees. GHD observes 9 holidays per year. Holiday pay will be based on the regular set schedule for the employee
Wellness Benefit- Regular full-term employees are eligible to participate in the wellness reimbursement program. GHD will reimburse 50% of the cost of the following to maximum of $250.00 reimbursement annually for such items as: Health club membership fees, Home exercise equipment purchases, Bicycles, Race, run & marathon entrance fees, Smoking cessation programs, Weight loss programs (i.e.—Weight Watchers, Jenny Craig), Fitbits and Fitness Tracking devices

Salary: $72,019 - $120,011, varies based on location and experience.

Take on some of the world’s toughest challenges - with everyone at GHD backing you every step of the way.

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

As a multicultural organization, we encourage individual achievement and recognize the strength of a diverse workforce. GHD is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description:
Joining our team provides the platform for growing your specialist career
You’ll be mentored by industry experts and manage projects for our clients
Perth, WA

An excellent opportunity to excel in the profession of Hazardous Materials & Occupational Hygiene; training and support from highly qualified professionals and a diverse range of projects on offer.

Why Join Our Team?

Joining our team means you’ll work alongside experienced scientists, engineers, and industry-leading consultants to deliver a broad range of complex hazardous materials projects.

We provide specialist services to several Tier 1 Mining and Oil & Gas companies, Defence, Federal and State government agencies, and several Tier 1 Mining and Oil & Gas companies.

Our project line-up includes some of the biggest and most iconic projects in WA and the NT, as well as projects ranging across East Asia, Central Europe and South America.

Working closely with the Tetra Tech family of companies, we apply deep technical expertise and project management capability to tackle complex challenges, making sure our solutions are creative, practical and sustainable.

About the role

We have a busy project line up right across our national Workplace Health and Safety team and we’re growing the team to keep up!

In this role, you’ll expand on your knowledge and experience in undertaking hazmat and occupational hygiene site inspections, engaging with clients and contractors, preparing technical reports and managing projects end-to-end.

We lead with science and ensure our solutions are tailored to fit each project. The sectors we work in are diverse and span mining, oil & gas, public infrastructure, future energy, defence and beyond!

You will be responsible for:

Hazardous materials/asbestos assessments and inspections
Occupational hygiene monitoring and asbestos fibre counting
Managing field programs for a range of Built Environment investigations
Observing, guiding, and recording site remediation activities
Data management, interpretation, and quality assurance/quality control
Assisting with writing proposals, project correspondence and technical reports

About you

To thrive in the role, you'll need:

Qualifications in related science disciplines and/or occupational hygiene
Demonstrable experience in the Hazardous Materials and/or Occupational Hygiene field
Strong project management skills with a focus on quality and delivery
Great communication, client relationship and teamwork skills
The ability to travel to regional and country sites as required
A commitment to safe, environmentally responsible project delivery
Hold a full Australian driver’s license
Be an Australian permanent resident or citizen (required for the Department of Defence)

Being a Licensed Asbestos Assessor, or eligible to apply within the near future, will be a distinct advantage.

This role is likely to include travel and remote work, including shifts away from home.

What You’ll Gain:

Support and coaching from our Practice Leader and renowned Subject Matter Experts
Career pathways with opportunities to deepen your technical capability and expand into leadership roles
A flexible work environment that supports your personal and professional goals
Access to diverse, high-profile projects across multiple sectors and geographies, including the possibility for international travel.

The Perks You’ll Love:

Work-Life Balance: Flexible work options, tailored hours, study breaks, and the ability to buy extra leave—up to 8 weeks per year!
Diverse Projects: Work across a wide variety of projects, clients, and sectors
Growth Opportunities: Professional development, coaching, and mentorship from our top experts
Memberships: Professional memberships to help you stay ahead in your field
Recognition: Our reward and recognition program makes sure your hard work doesn’t go unnoticed
Ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan
Parental Leave: Paid leave for both primary and secondary caregivers
Support: Employee assistance program for you and your immediate family
Travel Discounts: Great deals through our corporate traveller program
Car Leasing: Take advantage of novated vehicle leasing options

About us

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global 1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is actively seeking a talented Environmental Project/Program Manager for immediate employment in our Oakland, California office. In this role, you will be making a positive impact in the community through rewarding projects within our Environmental Practices.

This hybrid position (office and remote) requires the ideal candidate to demonstrate experience in regulatory and client engagement on complex sites, as well as investigation and remediation project experience, all while maintaining a strong emphasis on health and safety. new_jobs.title: Water Resources Market Leader
new_jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re looking for a place to advance your career, where you can contribute to a dynamic innovative firm, tackle demanding project work, and collaborate with industry recognized professionals – Geosyntec Consultants is the place for you!

Geosyntec
is seeking a Principal level Water Resources Market Leader
to join our growing national Water Resources Practice, based out of our Los Angeles, CA
;
San Diego, CA;
Sacramento, CA; Lakewood, CO
or any of our other U.S. based offices. The potential to work remotely from your home-office is available at the discretion of the Company. This is a unique opportunity to join a leadership team actively engaged in growing the water business at Geosyntec. This position will be responsible for developing and implementing a strategy for achieving significant market share for Geosyntec in the Water Resources market area.

As a senior member of our Water Resources practice, you lead complex water resources projects around water supply management, water rights permitting, and groundwater / surface water management. As a market leader, you will be responsible for a combination of technical project execution, client relationship management and water resource subject matter expertise, task and team leadership, while actively engaging existing and new client opportunities from a business development growth standpoint. Our Water Resources group works on complex projects ranging from water supply development, water supply management, water rights, mining hydrogeology, contaminant hydrogeology, regulatory permitting, and source water protection, across the U.S.; In this role, you will have the opportunity to build and lead a team of experienced professionals, contribute to complex technical project work, as well as actively engage in growth and business development strategy.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic business planning to segment and target specific industrial, commercial and municipal clients for projects such as water supply, groundwater and surface water modeling, water availability, use and re-use, as well as regulatory considerations for water rights permitting; focused on the West Region Water Resources market;
Engagement with project and operations staff to align Geosyntec’s full service delivery capabilities with market demands;
Serve in the capacity of a Client Account Manager on selected accounts deemed critical to Geosyntec’s Water Resources market;
Active participation in professional societies, conferences, and meetings that will increase the visibility of the firm to potential clients and recruits. Make contributions to the profession that will result in individual recognition as an industry leader;
Project directorship, including ensuring client expectations are understood and met, budgets are adhered to, quality objectives are met, and follow-on work is attainted – Strategically related to; local scale hydrogeologic analyses for water supply management, regulatory compliance and new source development; modeling studies of aquifer systems; installation and testing of groundwater supply wells (and monitoring wells), aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) and surface recharge basin projects, and permitting and regulatory compliance projects, including water rights;
Recruiting, managing, and mentoring junior staff and mid-career engineers and scientists;
Reviewing and leading the preparation of major proposals;
Providing senior leadership subject matter expertise in meetings with clients, regulatory personnel, and other parties;
Technical Project delivery and project-manager responsibility for scoping, performing, managing, and delivering multiple concurrent project assignments;
Preparing technical reports, letters, memoranda, plans, specifications, and proposals
Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor's degree in Water Resources, Hydrogeology, Civil, Environmental or related engineering discipline with emphasis on water resources. (required)
Advanced degree in the same/similar (preferred)
Professional registration (i.e., PE, CHG) (required)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At least 10 years (15+ preferred) of direct water resources, hydrogeology, or engineering consulting experience working on water resource, contaminated sites, and mining projects; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Experience with multi-disciplinary project teams. (required)
Demonstrated success in project management, sales, and business development. (required)
Excellent leadership and detail-orientation skills. (required)

Ability and willingness to perform fieldwork and travel as needed. (required)

new_jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Specialist
new_jobs.description:
About the Company

Trinity Consultants’ Monitoring Services team is hiring a Senior Air Quality Specialist to install, maintain, and troubleshoot ambient air quality and meteorological monitoring networks for clients across the country. This is a hands-on, field-first role for someone who takes pride in precise, defensible data. You’ll work directly with clients, travel to active monitoring sites, and be trusted to make real-time calls on equipment and data quality.

Schedule & Travel

Hybrid role based between the office and the field; ability to travel 2–5 days a week (transportation provided or compensated). Monday–Friday schedule; occasional weekend work may be required.

Field Operations & Installation

Conduct onsite installation, startup, and commissioning of meteorological and ambient air quality monitoring equipment.
Draw upon hands-on technical experience to perform analyzer maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibrations at remote monitoring sites, minimizing downtime and data loss.
Collect and operate time-integrated samples, and provide proper chain-of-custody documentation to analytical laboratories.
Apply practical field experience to support the design, integration, and build-out of ambient air quality monitoring systems.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

Maintain current audit and calibration certifications, and apply working knowledge of EPA and state monitoring protocols in the field.
Provide QA of air quality audit and calibration reports.
Review incoming data with an experienced eye to proactively flag instrumentation issues before they affect data quality.
Provide proper documentation and record keeping for all air quality systems and network servicing and auditing.

Client & Program Support

Provide meteorological sensor and air quality instrument calibration, maintenance, and audit services for numerous clients across the U.S., with a concentration in California.

Qualifications

4–8+ years of hands-on field experience in ambient air quality or meteorological monitoring; a Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, meteorology, or engineering may be considered in place of equivalent field experience.

Required Skills

Demonstrated, practical experience with DC electronics, telemetry, and remote data logging equipment.
Working knowledge of state and Federal (EPA) environmental monitoring guidelines and regulations, gained through direct application at active monitoring sites.
Hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience.
Strong work ethic, attention to detail, and proven problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Skills

Proven, hands-on experience operating and maintaining meteorological and air quality instrumentation.
Experience-based client interaction and communication skills, including strong active listening developed through direct client-facing field work.
Proficiency in the MS365 ecosystem (Teams, SharePoint, OneNote, etc.).

Pay range and compensation package

Our Santa Clarita office offers the stability of a corporate company with the atmosphere and camaraderie of a small, family-run business. We’re intentional about cultivating a fun, healthy environment for our team.

Competitive pay
401(k)
Dental insurance
Health insurance
Life insurance
Paid time off
Paid travel time, expenses, and daily per diem

Equal Opportunity Statement

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of duties. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to lift 70 lbs, travel freely and frequently, and remain on feet for up to 12 hours per day at field sites; multi-day field efforts are not uncommon. While performing site work, employees may occasionally be exposed to moving mechanical parts, high or precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, and toxic or caustic chemicals. Noise levels at monitoring sites are typically moderate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken. Comfort with basic math and algebra as applied to air quality measurements (percentages, area, volume, and similar calculations). Sound judgment interpreting instructions and troubleshooting variable field conditions where standardization is limited.

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Are you ready to lead a dynamic team of Emergency Response/Preparedness and environmental professionals in tackling some of the most pressing challenges facing our environment today?

Who are we looking for?

As a Project Manager
at GHD, you will not only mentor and guide the team but also take the reins in environmental emergencies, collaborating closely with clients and agencies to ensure effective response and resolution.

Your role will extend beyond project management to include business development and client expansion activities, where your expertise in environmental engineering, geology, or related fields will shine. With 5+ years of project management experience under your belt, including a proven track record in emergency response, client relationship management, and business development, you'll bring a wealth of knowledge to the table.

From conducting environmental sampling and monitoring to spearheading regional visibility initiatives, your passion for environmental stewardship and problem-solving will drive our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, possess exceptional communication skills, and are committed to making a difference, join us in shaping a sustainable future. Apply today and Join our Emergency Management (GHD FIRST) team.

This opportunity can be based out of the Chicago office.

Who is GHD FIRST:

GHD Fast Incident Response Services Team (GHD FIRST) delivers turnkey, 24/7/365 incident response and management services throughout North America. The GHD FIRST team provides the following core services:

Emergency Preparedness, Planning, and Drills
Environmental/ Remediation Services
Incident Management / Incident Command System (ICS)
Air Monitoring/ Industrial Hygiene
Waste Management
Toxicology/ Risk Assessment
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)/ Database
Shoreline Clean-up Assessment Technique (SCAT)
Digital Technology/ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Services
Construction/ Construction Management Services
Crisis Communication and Community Engagement
Litigation Support

GHD has more than 100 offices across North America with over 500 staff trained in emergency response and emergency management procedures. Listed below is a management role currently open to grow and further develop the GHD FIRST business sector within GHD.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Accountable for one or more medium-sized projects of low to moderate complexity with a small- to medium-sized team. Focus on the creation of the project vision and planning documents and manage the implementation, reporting, and performance of the overall project with the expectation of delivering on time, within budget, and to scope.

Document Preparation: Prepare moderately complex documents using a variety of applications for technology devices, such as standard office software. Also responsible for gathering and summarizing data for reports.
Stakeholder Management: Plan and deliver stakeholder engagement activities to develop effective working relationships for projects and to ensure that stakeholder needs and concerns are identified and met.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Continuous Improvement: Contribute to reviewing existing operations in own area of work, and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements.
Work Scheduling and Allocation: Assign short-term work schedules to a team of subordinates in order to achieve expectations while following established timelines.
Project Assurance: Conduct assurance reviews within the project, facilitate the delivery of assurance reviews by independent third parties, and take appropriate action to resolve any issues identified, so that senior stakeholders have confidence that the project can deliver according to time, budget, and quality.
Project Scope Definition: Manage the delivery of research, workshops, and other activities to support the specification and agreement of project deliverables.
Project Planning: Produce workstream or project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, are appropriately organized to deliver project objectives, and comply with the organization's project management framework.
Project Reporting and Review: Draft project review reports and presentations, including key information, commentary, and recommendations, to support the review process and enable stakeholders to evaluate progress and agree on change.
Project Resource Management: Manage the deployment of project resources, proactively managing project costs, providing forecasts, and presenting variances with narrative at appropriate review points to ensure effective utilization.
Project Risk and Issue Management: Identify and evaluate risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints associated with the project, escalating matters where appropriate. Where necessary, develop, agree on, and implement solutions to overcome these concerns.
Project Closeout and Handover: Draft elements of product documentation and user training to support handover to business as usual. Contribute to post-project reviews and identification of lessons learned.
Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.
Willingness to respond to call outs during non-routine working hours
Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or a related field

Experience

General Experience: Experience enables job holder to deal with the majority of situations and to advise others (Over 3 years to 6 years)
Managerial Experience: Experience of general supervision of more junior colleagues (7 to 12 months)
Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA
Experience with railroad and pipeline related emergencies a plus

Benefits:

401K - Employees are eligible to participate on the first day of the month following 3 months of service
Paid time off – Our PTO benefit is designed to provide eligible employees with a period of rest and relaxation, sick, and personal time throughout the year. PTO starts at 16 days per year and increases with years of service
Holiday Pay - Holiday pay is provided for eligible employees. GHD observes 9 holidays per year. Holiday pay will be based on the regular set schedule for the employee
Wellness Benefit- Regular full-term employees are eligible to participate in the wellness reimbursement program. GHD will reimburse 50% of the cost of the following to maximum of $250.00 reimbursement annually for such items as: Health club membership fees, Home exercise equipment purchases, Bicycles, Race, run & marathon entrance fees, Smoking cessation programs, Weight loss programs (i.e.—Weight Watchers, Jenny Craig), Fitbits and Fitness Tracking devices
